object.definition: Each action is $x_t\in[0,1]$, with fixed initial history $x_{1-m:0}=0$. Memory length $m\ge2$ includes the current action; two previous actions plus the current one correspond to $m=3$. $$f_t:[0,1]^m\to\mathbb R\ \text{is convex quadratic},\qquad |f_t(z)|\le B,\qquad\|\nabla f_t(z)\|_2\le L\quad(\forall z\in[0,1]^m).$$ The coefficients of $f_t$ may depend on history through $t-m$, but not more recent actions.

operation.query_signature: Choose $x_t$ using only past scalar feedback, then observe the realized memory loss $f_t(x_{t-m+1:t})$ without gradients. protocols.past_requery: History may be stored. New information from old samples or past rounds is unavailable unless the native interface explicitly permits it.
steps: The algorithm chooses $x_t$ using past scalar feedback and then observes the realized memory loss $f_t(x_{t-m+1:t})$. No gradient is returned.
There is no additional measurement noise beyond the randomness of the environment and algorithm.
Causal randomized policies must always act in $[0,1]$. The data $T,m,B,L$ and initial history are public; quadratic coefficients are hidden.

Received feedback may be stored and reused in computation. Unrevealed information cannot be requested from past rounds, and consumed random samples cannot receive additional queries. Current-round exceptions are limited to the explicitly supplied full-function access or same-sample two-point interface.

variable_blocks.dimension: Current-round length is $1$; memory-window length is $m$.
variable_blocks.space: The scalar action is $x_t\in[0,1]$. The loss depends on the most recent $m$ actions.
